title: Data Gaps, Flat Lines, Contradictions & Uncertainty

content.overview: Missing or contradictory environmental data reduce certainty but do not justify inventing replacements. Specialists preserve the original record, identify the limitation and use independent evidence where possible.

vocabulary.definition: A period or interval with missing expected measurements.
An implausibly unchanged signal that may indicate sensor, logging, configuration or communication failure.
A documented description of what the available evidence cannot support.

sections.title: Do not silently impute facts
sections.body: A gap overlapping a suspected excursion must remain a gap unless an approved reconstruction method exists. Use corroborating evidence without presenting estimates as measurements.

sections.title: Impossible patterns are evidence too
sections.body: Sudden flat lines, step changes or contradictions can indicate device, signal, configuration or logging faults and should trigger verification.

sections.title: Preserve competing evidence
sections.body: Do not delete readings merely because they conflict with a preferred interpretation. Record the conflict and the method used to decide which data are fit for use.

workedExamples: A two-hour data gap covers a suspected humidity spike; the report should state the missing interval and rely on alarms, neighboring verified sensors or equipment logs without fabricating values.
commonMistakes: Filling gaps with the nearest reading as fact.
Calling one successful spot check proof that intermittent faults are resolved.
content.practicalApplication: Review a trend containing a gap, flat line and disagreement, then classify each issue and write the uncertainty statement.
content.summary: Data-quality problems should be made visible, not repaired cosmetically.
